questions.prompt: A researcher asks whether the number of tutoring sessions a student attends predicts the student’s quiz score. Which variables are the independent and dependent variables?

options.label: A
options.text: Independent variable: quiz score; dependent variable: tutoring sessions

options.label: B
options.text: Independent variable: tutoring sessions; dependent variable: quiz score

options.label: D
options.text: The variables cannot be identified from the question

support.hint: Identify the predictor first, then the outcome it is being used to predict.

stuck.introduction: Read the research question as a proposed direction of explanation.
steps: Complete the sentence: the researcher uses variation in ___ to predict variation in ___.
Match the predictor to the independent or explanatory variable and the outcome to the dependent variable.
Check the options against those roles without assuming that prediction alone establishes causation.

questions.prompt: Researchers find that students who attend tutoring tend to earn higher grades. Students with stronger prior academic preparation may also be more likely to attend tutoring. Why might researchers control for prior academic preparation?

options.label: A
options.text: To determine whether tutoring is still related to grades after differences in prior preparation are taken into account

options.label: B
options.text: To make all students academically equivalent

options.label: C
options.text: To ensure that tutoring causes higher grades

options.label: D
options.text: To remove students with lower grades from the study

support.hint: Prior preparation could be related to both attending tutoring and earning higher grades.

stuck.introduction: Think about what makes a tutoring comparison fair.
steps: Identify tutoring attendance as the factor of interest and grades as the outcome.
Consider how different prior preparation could influence both the likelihood of attending tutoring and the resulting grades.
Ask what comparing students with similar prior preparation would help the researcher investigate, and avoid treating statistical control as a guarantee of causation.
